title: I’m building a Vampire Survivors-style game with AI, but this time you play as the villain. Free demo is out!
author: Plastic_Bag6171
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been working on **Darkfall**, a dark fantasy horde-survival roguelite built with the help of AI.

The idea is simple: instead of playing the hero fighting endless waves of monsters, **you're the warlock that everyone is trying to kill.**

The main mechanic is necromancy. You can raise fallen enemies, turn them into your own undead army, and even bring defeated bosses back to fight for you.

One thing I've learned while developing with AI is that getting something playable is only the beginning. Making the mechanics feel good, balancing the combat, and keeping everything readable when the screen gets chaotic requires a lot of iteration.

That's what I'm focusing on now.

I've just released a **free 20-minute demo for Windows and Mac** on itch.io:

🎮 [https://adirz.itch.io/darkfall](https://adirz.itch.io/darkfall)

I'd love to hear from other AI game developers here. What's been your biggest challenge when turning an AI-assisted project into an actual playable game?

And if you try the demo, I'd really appreciate your feedback!

Still lots to improve, but I'm excited to finally share it.

comments.author: K_kkomi
comments.body:
I think one of the biggest challenges is making sure the core gameplay loop is actually fun, rather than just functional.

I'm also developing an indie game with Claude Code, and getting mechanics to work is often easier than making them feel satisfying. Balancing difficulty and figuring out where players might get confused takes a lot of iteration.

The villain perspective is a really cool twist on the genre, by the way. Good luck with Darkfall!

replies.author: Plastic_Bag6171
replies.body: I completely agree! There was a lot of back and forth with Claude Code, tons of testing, and many full playthroughs before I finally got the gameplay to where I wanted it. Getting things to work is one thing, but making them actually fun is a whole different challenge. Thanks, and good luck with your game too!

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Plastic_Bag6171 please add some details about how you used AI to develop this. Saying you used AI isn't enough on its own. We're looking for the actual dev details. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process and the actual development. We're trying to keep the sub from filling up with low quality game posts. If this doesn't get updated, it may be removed.

replies.author: Plastic_Bag6171
replies.body: Thanks for the heads-up! I've updated the post with more details about the AI development process.
